answer:
Marie Curie died of aplastic anemia on July 4, 1934, at age 66, at the Sancellemoz sanatorium in Passy, in the French Alps [1][2]. Aplastic anemia is a condition in which the bone marrow stops making enough blood cells. In her case it is attributed to years of exposure to radiation, both from handling radioactive materials in her research and from her work with mobile X-ray units during World War I [2][3]. Radiation's health risks were poorly understood at the time. She often carried radium samples in her pockets, and her papers are still radioactive today [2].
